final.investment_thesis:
The conflict in this debate is narrower than it looks, and where it exists the bear wins on timing while the bull wins on durability — which is precisely a Hold sized small, not a manufactured direction.

What the bear won, and it is not contested by anyone. AAPL closed 305.93 below the 50SMA (309.19), the 10EMA (309.46) and the VWMA (314.11); the 304.81–333.43 gap from the 2026-07-31 shock is entirely unfilled and constitutes a live overhead supply shelf; the 2026-08-14 session traded 28.2M shares, the lightest in roughly four months, so the bounce is volume-starved rather than accumulation; the MACD histogram has contracted for three sessions with a plausible 10/50 cross within one to three sessions. The aggressive analyst's proposed add trigger — 309.5 with >50M shares — sits 1.2% above spot, meaning the strongest bull in the room is himself unwilling to pay 305.93. That is the cleanest evidence in the packet: a constructive thesis that declines to buy at the current price is a Hold, not an Overweight.

What the bull won, and it is why this is not Underweight or Sell. The operating evidence is genuinely strong and was never dented: 16.4% revenue growth, 50.06% gross margin, operating margin expanding 152bp through a 32.5% R&D ramp, $62.2B of net cash, and buybacks re-accelerating into weakness. Price at 305.93 sits 9.1% above a rising 200SMA at 280.48, so this is a correction inside an intact primary uptrend, not a structural break. My own record binds here: six prior AAPL Underweights (07-20 through 07-24, plus 07-31 at −2.1% alpha) each bled 3.2% to 13.6% of five-day alpha by trimming inside a stacked rising trend on momentum-decay logic, and the 07-31 reflection codified the fix — require a second confirmation (a close below 300, or continued relative weakness) before staging further trims. That confirmation has not printed. Cutting the residual core into an unfilled gap, above a rising 200SMA, with no broken fundamental, would repeat the exact error the record punishes.

The 2026-08-07 lesson is the counterweight and it is why the size is 2.95% and not larger. That Hold at 60–65% of a standard allocation lost 2.7% of five-day alpha into this same tape. The correct inference is not 'sell everything' — it is that mid-single-digit-to-low-double-digit exposure was the wrong size for a name sitting under an 8.6% overnight gap with no confirmation. The position has already been reduced to the size the evidence supports. Applying another proportional discount to 2.95% would be mechanical trimming without a fresh total-target justification, which is explicitly not warranted here.

Sizing, with the alternatives stated concretely. A higher allocation of 7–10% of total equity would put roughly $7,000–$10,000 into a name sitting directly beneath a 304.81–333.43 supply shelf with ~8% gap risk — about 0.6%–0.8% of total equity at risk for roughly 0.9%–1.2% of upside to the gap ceiling, an asymmetry that only turns favorable after the 309.5 volume reclaim. A lower allocation of 0% is feasible but worse: it forfeits long-term compounding and the unpriced China AI / fall iPhone catalyst, and pays round-trip fees for zero informational gain. The retained 2.95% is not an unspecified observation position — observation does not require holding stock. It is a deliberately cheap convex position: an 8% adverse move costs roughly 0.25% of total equity, a 12% recovery adds roughly 0.4%, and a gap-up on an unpriced catalyst is captured at full participation. That purpose is preferable to zero precisely because the cost of carrying it is smaller than the cost of being absent when the catalyst prints.

Cash opportunity cost is weighed, not waved away. 97.05% of the account ($96,905.54) earns no interest, and a gap-up through 333.43 would cost the book real relative return. That is the argument for adding — but it is an argument that activates at 309.5 on volume, where the overhead shelf becomes support instead of resistance. Paying for that optionality now, before the shelf is absorbed, converts an opportunity cost into a realized loss.

What would change the call. Upgrade to Overweight and raise the total target to 5–6% on a daily close above 309.5 on >50M shares, scaling further only on acceptance above 320–333.43 with volume confirming July supply has been absorbed. Downgrade to Underweight and cut toward zero on a daily close below 280.5 (200SMA), with the next structural references below that; also downgrade on an FQ4 print showing gross margin materially below 49.5% with revenue growth decelerating. The 280.5 line is ~25 points (~3.2x ATR of 7.86) below spot — a strategic trend stop, not a noise-level stop, and it is a narrative condition, not an implemented order.

Data gaps, stated plainly rather than papered over: there is no news coverage of 2026-08-07 through 2026-08-12, the sample is 20 of 223 records, the MFI units are ambiguous, no options chain or implied-volatility data was supplied (so any collar or put protection cannot be priced from this evidence set), and no consensus estimates, forward multiples or Q4 guidance figures are in the record. The 330 target below is therefore technical (gap-fill proximity), not valuation-derived, and no calibrated probability is assigned to either the upside or downside scenario.
